The Owners Playbook by Richard Vaughton When revenue drops, the first thing an owner asks is simple: “Why?” It sounds like a straightforward question. But anyone managing short-term rentals knows it rarely has a simple answer. Revenue rarely declines for just one reason. It is usually a mix of shifting demand, pricing pressure, occupancy dips, guest experience issues, or broader market changes. The challenge is not a lack of data—it is the time and effort required to turn that data into a clear, confident explanation. For one property, that might take hours. Across a portfolio, it becomes unsustainable. And that is where problems begin. Because when owners do not hear from you, they start forming their own conclusions. The job is not reporting. It is explanation. The best property managers are not just operators. They are translators of performance. They do not wait for questions. They answer them before they are asked. As Richard Vaughton highlights, the opportunity is not just better reporting: it is better communication, delivered with context, clarity, and timing. This is where an AI-powered owner playbook comes in. BAM brings together revenue performance, market dynamics, guest feedback, and operational signals, and turns them into a clear narrative of what is happening and why. Not raw data. Not dashboards. Explanation. From reactive updates to proactive trust Most owner communication is reactive. Monthly summaries. Quarterly reviews. Conversations triggered by underperformance. By that point, the narrative is already forming and you are responding to it. With an AI-powered playbook, that dynamic shifts. Owners receive regular, evidence-backed updates that show you are actively managing the property, even when performance fluctuates. They see the context behind the numbers. They understand the decisions being made. And that changes everything. You are no longer defending results. You are guiding the conversation. Hospitality is about people — the guests we serve and the professionals we empower. We built this because we needed it. Boom did not start in a lab. It started in a South Florida property management company that had outgrown its own tooling. The company was scaling, and the stack was not. Guest messages arrived faster than anyone could answer them. Rates were set on a spreadsheet on Sunday night and left alone all week. Housekeeping ran on WhatsApp. The month-end close took days, and by the time an owner statement went out, the month it described was already gone. Every tool on the market promised to help. What they actually did was draft — a suggested reply, a suggested rate, a suggested task — and then wait for somebody to click. That is not leverage. That is a queue with better manners. jobs.description: Back to all roles Sales Development Representative Apply Job details S&M / Sales United States, EU Full-time Boom is seeking a motivated and energetic Sales Development Representative (SDR) to help fuel our growth. As an SDR, you will be on the front lines of our sales efforts — generating, qualifying, and nurturing leads for our Account Executives. This role is ideal for someone early in their sales career who is eager to learn, thrives in a fast-paced startup environment, and is excited about building relationships with prospective customers. Key Responsibilities: Research, identify, and engage potential prospects through outbound outreach (email, phone, LinkedIn, etc.). Qualify inbound leads and schedule discovery calls or product demos for Account Executives. Maintain a consistent pipeline of qualified opportunities through diligent prospecting efforts. Understand customer needs and effectively communicate Boom’s value proposition. Collaborate with Account Executives and the Sales VP to develop prospecting strategies. Log all activities, notes, and interactions in the CRM system to ensure accurate pipeline tracking. Achieve or exceed weekly and monthly activity metrics (calls, emails, meetings booked).
